sections.text:
Elias, peace be upon him, is a noble prophet from the children of Israel. God sent him to a people who live in the city of Baalbek in the Levant.

His people had deviated greatly from the worship of God who created them, abandoned the teachings of the previous prophets, and began worshiping a huge idol known at that time called “Baal.”

They would offer sacrifices to this idol, ask for sustenance and rain, build great temples for it, and spend their money pleasing the priests who served it.

Prophet Elias, peace be upon him, stood bravely in their midst, calling on them to abandon these superstitions and return to the worship of the One and Only God.

He said to them in a tone full of denunciation and reproach, as mentioned in the Holy Qur’an: “Do you call upon Baal and forsake the best of creators? God is your Lord and the Lord of your forefathers.”

Elias was trying to awaken their dead minds; How can they abandon God, who created them and their fathers, and worship a stone that does not hear, benefit, or harm?
But the people, instead of listening to the call of reason, lied to him and ridiculed him, just as previous nations had done with their prophets.

Not only did they deny it, but they incited their mighty king to kill him, so they began to chase him everywhere to get rid of him and his calling, which was disturbing their comfort and threatening the authority of the priests.

Elias, peace be upon him, was forced to leave the city in order to protect his life and the lives of the few vulnerable people who believed with him.

Elias hid in the mountains and barren caves for several years, enduring hunger, thirst, and the cruelty of nature, but God was with him, protecting him and providing for him.

Meanwhile, Elias prayed to his Lord to prevent rain from his people, so that they might consider and realize that the idol “Baal” had no control over the matter.

God answered his prayer, and the rain stopped for three consecutive years! The rivers dried up, crops perished, livestock died, and drought and famine spread throughout Baalbek.

People rushed to their idol, “Baal,” praying to him and offering him the most precious offerings, but the idol remained silent, unable to move, and not bringing a single drop of water.

They finally realized the powerlessness of their idol, so they went back looking for Elias, and when they found him, they asked him to pray to God to lift this affliction from them, and they promised him that they would believe.

Elijah called upon his Lord, and heavy rain fell, the earth turned green, and life returned again, but unfortunately they soon broke their covenant and returned to worshiping idols!
Elias was angry at their stubbornness and their broken promises, and he prayed to his Lord to relieve him of them and their disbelief.

God told Elias that their torment would inevitably occur, and that God would grant him victory and raise him up.

Elias continued his preaching and his movement between villages, until he met a good young man called “Elisha”, who believed in him and stayed with him like his shadow, and learned wisdom and religion from him.

Elias left the matter of the call to his successor, Elisha, to continue the journey after him among the Children of Israel.

God mentioned Elias in the Holy Qur’an, praising him and giving him good tidings of peace: “Peace be upon the family of Yasin. * Indeed, thus do We reward the doers of good.”

The lesson of the story of Elias, peace be upon him, is that truth is victorious, even after a while, and that attachment to material things or people (such as idols in our time) is no substitute for God’s grace in times of adversity.
